claims.statement: Directive (EU) 2024/3019 requires Member States to establish extended producer responsibility for products in Annex III by 31 December 2028 and assigns producers at least 80% of specified quaternary-treatment and monitoring costs, subject to the directive's rules.

contrary_evidence: National implementation and cost-allocation rules are not yet uniform, so a 2026 product may be early and exemptions may reduce the fee pool.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a rights-separated mapping of public substance evidence, national allocation precedents, and anonymized case outcomes improves defense quality
fingerprint.customer: small and mid-sized EU pharmaceutical and cosmetic producers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: environmental law firms, laboratories, and industry associations refer assessments
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: secure substance mapping, exemption tests, allocation audit, evidence dossier, and counsel-ready challenge support
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the producer pays at annual assessment preparation and on a verified reduction or successful appeal
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a national producer-responsibility body calculates or invoices the producer's share of quaternary wastewater-treatment costs

founder_fit: Strong analytics and EU-regulation fit, but employer conflicts require a written exclusion, no Reckitt data, and independent legal review before launch.
risks: Handling formulations creates trade-secret and conflict-of-interest risk.
Success fees may be restricted in some professional-service arrangements.

structure.control_point: the auditable product and substance evidence packet used to calculate, exempt, or contest a producer's EPR charge
structure.critical_dependency: national transposition, allocation methodology, producer-authorized formulation data, and defensible analytical methods

thesis: Build a product-composition and exemption evidence service for smaller pharmaceutical and cosmetic producers facing national allocation of urban-wastewater micropollutant treatment costs. The paid trigger is an annual EPR assessment or appeal, with no use of the founder's employer confidential information. All commercial numbers, including capital_required_pln, are unvalidated hypotheses.
title: Micropollutant EPR Cost-Allocation Defense Bureau
uncertainties: National methodologies and first invoice dates are unknown.
SME willingness to share composition data is unvalidated.
